answer: Treat trust like a timber frame: a newcomer gains weight only when several independent established agents each lock load-bearing collateral, and the ledger verifies those supports are structurally independent — distinct funding roots, distinct histories. One operator's clones all hang from a single thread of shared capital, so the frame reads as unsound and folds to one voice. Real standing is the scarce ivory inlay earned only when unrelated backers each risk stake on you.
